evidence.claim: Marcos presented human welfare as a governing priority, saying the DSWD would lead support for people most in need, that no one would be left behind, and that the administration would use social-protection programs for those needing help.
evidence.title: State of the Nation Address of His Excellency Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. President of the Philippines to the Congress of the Philippines
evidence.excerpt: Marcos presented human welfare as a governing priority, saying the DSWD would lead support for people most in need, that no one would be left behind, and that the administration would use social-protection programs for those needing help.
evidence.source_locator: first SONA passages on social protection, vulnerable sectors, and DSWD-led assistance
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential speech text is strong evidence of policy intent and stated priorities, though not of delivery by itself.
evidence.period_fit: Direct target-year speech delivered on July 25, 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as his own policy statement within presidential authority.
contrary_evidence: This is a speech of intent, not proof of execution.
It relies on promised programs rather than audited outcomes.

evidence.claim: The DOH said it had accelerated COVID-19 vaccination and booster rollout, sustained testing, strengthened detection and isolation systems, and reinvigorated Universal Health Care safety nets for poor and vulnerable groups in accordance with President Marcos's first-100-days directives.
evidence.title: DOH achieves major strides in fight vs COVID-19, strengthens PH healthcare system
evidence.excerpt: The DOH said it had accelerated COVID-19 vaccination and booster rollout, sustained testing, strengthened detection and isolation systems, and reinvigorated Universal Health Care safety nets for poor and vulnerable groups in accordance with President Marcos's first-100-days directives.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and list of actions under Marcos directives
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official health-department release is strong for the policy actions described, though not independently for effectiveness.
evidence.period_fit: Direct target-year 2022 implementation under Marcos's first 100 days.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable in part to Marcos because the release explicitly ties the actions to his directives.
contrary_evidence: The release is self-reported by the implementing agency.
It describes actions and system strengthening rather than measured outcomes.

evidence.claim: DepEd said the school calendar was issued in line with its commitment to resume five days of in-person classes, with all public and private schools transitioning back to in-person learning by November 2, 2022.
evidence.title: DepEd releases guidelines for School Year 2022-2023
evidence.excerpt: DepEd said the school calendar was issued in line with its commitment to resume five days of in-person classes, with all public and private schools transitioning back to in-person learning by November 2, 2022.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs on school calendar and transition back to in-person classes
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official education guidance is strong evidence for the policy choice and timetable.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year education policy enacted in July 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Marcos administration through the education department, though the order itself was signed by the vice president and education secretary.
contrary_evidence: This is a reopening and delivery measure, not evidence of learning gains.
Implementation quality could still vary by school and region.

evidence.claim: In Marcos's first 100 days, DBM said it approved billions in assistance for rice farmers, the most vulnerable households affected by inflation, calamity victims, commuters, and healthcare workers, including P5,000 subsidies for more than 1.5 million rice farmers.
evidence.title: DBM releases billions of pesos to aid rice farmers, vulnerable households, calamity victims, commuters, healthcare workers in the first 100 days of Marcos Jr Administration
evidence.excerpt: In Marcos's first 100 days, DBM said it approved billions in assistance for rice farmers, the most vulnerable households affected by inflation, calamity victims, commuters, and healthcare workers, including P5,000 subsidies for more than 1.5 million rice farmers.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and subsidy details in the release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official budget-management release is strong evidence for the program rollout and intended beneficiaries.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and Marcos's first 100 days in office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the Marcos administration because the release describes first-100-days policy execution under his presidency.
contrary_evidence: It is an administrative release, not an independent audit of effectiveness.
The aid is responsive relief, not structural poverty reduction by itself.

evidence.claim: Marcos placed several regions under a state of calamity after Severe Tropical Storm Paeng, directing agencies to continue rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and price-control measures and to augment basic services in affected areas.
evidence.title: PBBM declares state of calamity in ‘Paeng’-hit regions
evidence.excerpt: Marcos placed several regions under a state of calamity after Severe Tropical Storm Paeng, directing agencies to continue rescue, relief, rehabilitation, and price-control measures and to augment basic services in affected areas.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential release is strong for the decision and its stated purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos as head of state exercising calamity powers.
contrary_evidence: The declaration is a response measure, not proof of successful recovery.
Its effect depends on later implementation by agencies and LGUs.

evidence.claim: Marcos signed the 2023 national budget in December 2022 and identified education, public works, health, social welfare, agriculture, and transportation as the priority sectors of his administration's first national budget.
evidence.title: PBBM signs P5.2 trillion 2023 national budget
evidence.excerpt: Marcos signed the 2023 national budget in December 2022 and identified education, public works, health, social welfare, agriculture, and transportation as the priority sectors of his administration's first national budget.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs on the 2023 budget and priority sectors
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary budget-signing release is strong evidence for the administration's stated spending priorities and legislative support.
evidence.period_fit: Target-year action at the end of 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Marcos because he signed and described the first budget of his administration.
contrary_evidence: Budget priority is not the same as actual service delivery.
Spending outcomes depend on execution and procurement after enactment.

evidence.claim: Within 100 days, the PinasLakas campaign had administered 3,456,132 first booster doses and vaccinated 47,803 senior citizens, with almost 73.3 million Filipinos fully vaccinated by Oct. 10, 2022.
evidence.title: PinasLakas administers 3.4M 1st booster dose in 100 days
evidence.excerpt: Within 100 days, the PinasLakas campaign had administered 3,456,132 first booster doses and vaccinated 47,803 senior citizens, with almost 73.3 million Filipinos fully vaccinated by Oct. 10, 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Government newswire reports exact rollout figures and date-stamped accomplishments.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to Marcos's first 100 days.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial-to-strong: Marcos publicly directed the booster push, while DOH/DILG and local implementers executed the rollout.
contrary_evidence: This is rollout volume, not direct proof of health outcome gains or equity of coverage.

evidence.claim: UNICEF reported that classes had moved to full face-to-face modality, around 94 percent of Filipinos were satisfied with school reopening, and DepEd was implementing the RAPID learning-recovery framework with staffing and literacy-assessment measures.
evidence.title: Full return to in-person classes another milestone in learning recovery
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF reported that classes had moved to full face-to-face modality, around 94 percent of Filipinos were satisfied with school reopening, and DepEd was implementing the RAPID learning-recovery framework with staffing and literacy-assessment measures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent UN-agency reporting with a survey result and implementation detail, though partly reliant on partner framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partial: this reflects the Marcos administration's reopening environment, but the article also notes continuing constraints and broad partner support.
contrary_evidence: UNICEF simultaneously warned that vulnerable children still needed support and that many public schools lacked minimum WASH facilities.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Marcos-attributed existential-risk choice, safeguard reform, or command-and-control decision is recoverable.
The package is heavy on nuclear-energy framing and treaty baseline, but thin on any ruler-attributed safety or precautionary implementation.
No hard 2022 finding of personal self-enrichment, hidden assets, procurement conflict, or office misuse by Marcos is present.
Several of the strongest items are campaign-ecosystem or staffing-pattern evidence rather than clean office-period personal conduct.
